To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Niagara XML-ql query language is a powerful and expressive language for XML query processing, and (2) the Niagara Internet Query System provides a powerful and flexible mechanism for processing queries over the Internet.

(a) the Niagara Internet Query System, which is a public domain system that can be obtained at http://www- db.cs.wisc.edu, provides the ability to query the Internet using the Niagara XML- QL query language and Niagara XML search engine; (b) the Niagara Internet Quesry System provides a mechanism to find relevant XML documents using a collaboration between the Niagara Internet Query Processor and the Niagara XML search engine.

(a) a novel collaboration between an XML query processor and an XML search engine enables the discovery of relevant XML files, (b) synchronization packets inserted at critical points in an operator tree guarantee the consistency of query results, and (c) the Niagara Internet Query System provides a practical and efficient mechanism for querying the Internet.

developing techniques and algorithms to support efficient query processing over XML files on the Internet.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the system is a prototype for an Internet query system that is able to process XML queries over the Internet.
we developed a query processing system for XML data that is capable of handling data sources that are infinite streams and/or have unpredictable access rates.
we have developed a system to support the querying of the Internet using XML query language, and we have demonstrated that it can scale up to the Internet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is not sufficient to merely provide an efficient XML query processor to query the Internet.
the design of an Internet query system must consider both the data and the sources.
the Internet is a very different environment from a conventional database.
